title: The full normalized characterization of the completed diagonal arrow
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $Y$ a scheme with $\ell$ invertible. Use the simultaneous derived reduction $D$ and strict Cartier system of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-system], and the completed coefficients, derived limits, source and target comparisons of [det-prop-diagonal-tower-limit], with that node's derived-category size conventions. A completed arrow $\delta:\Delta_*\Zl\to\Zl(1)[2]$ is a normalized diagonal limit when it admits exactly the full normalized data in the conclusion of the latter node: a root system $H$ with its root identification, the canonical single-functor source comparison, the signed boundary class and all finite positive Cartier normalizations; total derived limit and completed reduction data; ordinary source and root limit isomorphisms normalized by their canonical generators and projections; invertible derived-limit comparisons; derived completeness of both endpoints; the whole-system comparison equation for $\delta$ and its uniqueness for those comparisons; and the stated reduction comparisons at every finite level. The root-limit comparison is the actual composite of preservesLimitIso and HasLimit.isoOfNatIso. This is a predicate on an already specified arrow, not a choice from its finite evaluations.
